facts.value: Urban design is an interdisciplinary field that uses elements of many built environment professions.
Urban design includes elements from landscape architecture, urban planning, architecture, civil engineering, and municipal engineering.
Different subfields of urban design include strategic urban design, landscape urbanism, water-sensitive urban design, and sustainable urbanism.

Architecture sits between design, structure, space, use, and the realities that make buildings work over time. It deals with space, structure, light, movement, climate, use, and the way people actually live inside buildings over time.
At its core, architecture is about creating spaces that work, feel right, and hold up. Architecture is not just drawing buildings, engineering, or art; it combines all three.
Architecture is the art and science of designing buildings and other physical environments.

Architecture involves how people move through space, how light enters a room, how a building meets the ground, how a wall assembly holds up, how a plan supports daily life, and how a structure fits a climate, budget, and culture.
Architecture is broader than decoration and broader than construction alone.
A beginner mistake is treating architecture like a clean drawing problem; it is not.
Architecture is a coordination problem where structure, materials, weather, circulation, code, cost, and human use all push back at the same time.
The complexity of architecture is what makes it worth studying as it requires both technical constraints and imagination from the first sketch onward.

facts.value: Architecture keeps changing because the world keeps changing. Climate pressure, urban density, digital tools, adaptive reuse, smarter building systems, and new material questions are all reshaping the field. But the center of architecture has not changed much. It is still about making places that work, last, and mean something to the people using them.
